the difference between the far-field pattern generated by a cornered structure and that generated by the same structure with rounded corners is of order (kρ) ^{2} as the radius of the rounded corners decreases, and that the difference between these far-field patterns is due to a change in the phase and magnitude of the scattered wave at each point on the circumference of the rounded corner.
the difference in the far-field patterns between the cornered structure and the rounded corner is O((k ρ) ^{m} ) as ρ decreases, where the exponent m depends upon the type of boundary condition.

the difference in far-field patterns generated when the corners of a structure are rounded and when they are left sharp is O((k\rho)^m) where k is the wavenumber, \(\rho\) is the radius of curvature of the rounded corners, and m is the number of corners of the original structure.

the effect of rounding the corners of an infinite cylindrical structure on the far-field pattern generated when the structure is illuminated by a plane wave.
the scattering of a time-harmonic electromagnetic wave from a two-dimensional structure with corners.
the effect that rounding the corners of an infinite cylinder has on the scattering of a time-harmonic electromagnetic wave.

the far-field pattern generated by a cornered cylinder is the same as the far-field pattern for a rounded corner cylinder, provided the radius of curvature is small enough, and the cornered cylinder is sufficiently long.
